additional_info.subject: RE: ID0452671-DC/Si-D/DE-[Multi] Charging points out of service CRM:03056000032
additional_info.body:
Dear Marcel Doods,
I am reaching out in regards of ticket
ID0452671
. The ticket has been opened on your end for outlets being Out of Order in the morning of 25.09.2025 on chargers
170000665
and
170000666.
I analyzed the logs corresponding at the timestamps of your photos, and these are my findings:
Charger
170000666:
The charger had DC2 out of order while DC1 was charging.
From the logs, I could see a severe event of "error coap polling". This is an internal communication interruption between SECC and PLC. SiC D will reconnect to SECC within 5 seconds. While SECC is not reachable, the outlet will be set as unavailable or preparing.
This error is solved in the latest Sicharge D FW v8.0.5. I see from SCB that the charger is running on v6.0.3 (so 3 FW versions older). I would recommend to update the charger to the latest v8.0.5, in order to avoid this error coap polling to appear again.
If the update cannot be performed, in alternative a Hotfix can be installed upon the actual FW version.
Charger
170000665:
Both DC outlets were OoO since the previous time the charger booted up. Error flags in the logs showed:
The voltage transducer TF5 had an error and the charger could not configure the converter groups.
I performed a reserch in the logs over the last 2 weeks, and it seems that the error flags related to TF5 are appearing daily, setting the charger unable to configure.
For this reason, it is necessary to go onsite, verify the status of the High Voltage Transducer (power supply, connections, status of the clamps), and in case replace it.
In conclusion:
​​​​​​​
Mr. Doods: please provide me feedback in regards of the update of the charger to v8.0.5, or in case of the Hotfix if not possible. I will proceed with the update as soon as I will have the green light from your side.
Colleagues of RC-DE: it is necessary to go onsite and check for charger
MP / P6 170000665
according to the following scheme:
the connection of clamps WC10 and WC11
24V power supply to TF5
Signal between TF5 and PLC.
In case TF5 is defective, please procced with replacement
Looking forward to hearing feedback from you soon!
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
Smart Infrastructure

Expert Services

13629 Berlin, Germany
